subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — follow-up and details
messages:
From: Tom Harris <tom.harris@novalabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Leila Chen <leila.chen@novalabs.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — follow-up and details

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap from our side and a few data points to help with sizing: 

- Why Dedicated: compliance + predictable latency for our customer-facing assistant.
- Expected traffic: baseline ~15 TPS, peak bursts up to ~60–80 TPS (peaks last ~10–20 minutes).
- Model mix: primary model will be an in-house fine-tuned 70B (generate-heavy), secondary 13B for short queries.
- Token mix: ~65% short (<64 tokens total), ~25% medium (64-512), ~10% long (>512). Average end-to-end tokens per request ~350 (inputs + outputs).
- Concurrency target: we want to support ~30 concurrent sessions during peaks without queuing.
- Region: us-east-1 required for data residency.

Attached a small snapshot of current usage and a sample request distribution (prod-usage-snapshot.csv). Can you recommend a starting GPU configuration and any notes on caching/batching we should expect? Also pls include any constraints for private VPC vs hosted/dedicated options if relevant.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Harris
Head of Platform
Nova Labs

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Harris <tom.harris@novalabs.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-06T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — follow-up and details

Hi Tom — thanks for the detailed recap and the attachment, very helpful. High level thoughts based on the numbers you sent: 

- Model family matters a lot: 70B-class models (even quantized) are much heavier on memory and KV cache pressure. For ~60–80 TPS peak with ~350 avg tokens, we typically recommend either an H100-based pool (best latency/throughput) or an A100-80GB cluster with sharding and aggressive quantization.

Sizing options (starting points):
1) Performance option (latency-focused): 2x H100 nodes (or equivalent) with multi-GPU serving per model + KV cache; expected p95 intra-region latency ~200–300ms for 70B quantized generations at ~60 TPS with batching tuned. Supports your 30 concurrent sessions headroom.
2) Cost-optimized option: 4x A100-80GB (or 8x A10G depending on availability) with model sharding + quantization to 4-bit. Expected p95 ~400–600ms under peak; lower hourly cost but more engineering tradeoffs.

Operational notes:
- Batching and prefix/KV caching: with a high short-request percentage (65%), batching will be effective for throughput without adding much tail latency. We recommend a short batching window (5–10ms) and prefix caching for recurrent prompts.
- Token throughput: please confirm if the ~350 tokens estimate is weighted toward output or input-heavy; output-heavy workloads increase compute per request.
- Private VPC: Dedicated in a VPC is supported; we can surface a private control plane and VPC peering. Private on-prem would add network/ops lead time and typically requires additional sizing margins.

Next steps: I attached a short sizing template (redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx) — can you fill the model names, expected percent traffic per model, and any SLAs you need? If this looks good I’d like to loop Aditya (SE) to produce a preliminary capacity estimate and a runbook for rollout. 

Available for a 30-min follow-up on Wed 2026-08-11 at 10:00am PT — does that work?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Harris <tom.harris@novalabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Leila Chen <leila.chen@novalabs.com>
Date: 2026-08-06T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — follow-up and details

Thanks Marissa — that all makes sense. A few clarifications/fill-ins: 

- Model details: primary is our fine-tuned 70B (we'll call it nl-70b-ft), secondary is an open 13B family for quick responses. Expect traffic split ~70% nl-70b-ft, 30% 13B.
- Token breakdown: typical request = ~150 input tokens + ~200 output tokens => ~350 avg. Output-heavy for the 70B model (more generation).
- SLA: we'd like p95 latency < 500ms for the primary model during normal peaks; occasional higher tail during extreme spikes is acceptable.
- Networking/region: us-east-1 for production; staging can be in us-west. We prefer Dedicated (reserved) capacity in our VPC if possible.

I've uploaded a slightly larger sample (prod-usage-snapshot.csv) to the thread. We'll fill the sizing template tonight and get back before the follow-up. Wed 8/11 10:00am PT works for Leila + me.

Regards,
Tom

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Harris <tom.harris@novalabs.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-06T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — follow-up and details

Perfect — thanks for the clarifications, Tom. Attached is an initial high-level recommendation based on your prelim numbers and the distribution you shared. Quick summary: 

- Recommended starting config (preliminary): 2x H100 nodes dedicated to nl-70b-ft + 1x A100-80GB node pool for 13B traffic. This combination hits your p95 < 500ms target and gives headroom for bursts.
- Fallback/scale strategy: add 1 A100 node to the pool for burst windows and enable auto-burst to hosted capacity for extreme spikes.
- Caching/batching defaults: batching window 10ms, async KV cache for prompt prefixes, and request-level timeouts at 6s.

Aditya — can you take this and build a short capacity estimate (GPU counts, expected sustained QPS per GPU, and an hourly estimate) ahead of Wed's call? Tom/Leila — please upload the filled sizing template and any additional perf traces to the HubSpot link so we can iterate before the call: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/324
